posts:
Students boycott AI as neuroscientists warn of cognitive decay.
Evidence: Exam scores drop 20%, Grassroots protests, Data center backlash
#Aletheia #Education #AI

Studies show AI boosts homework scores by 18% but drops exam results by 20%, prompting neuroscientists to warn against offloading deep thinking.
Stated Judgement: (+0.9, +0.5) — Greater Good

Systemic over-reliance on generative AI erodes cognitive reserve and critical thinking, while students organize boycotts against data centers and automated tools.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -0.6) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Convenience masks cognitive degradation as educational systems fail to adapt to generative tools.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 4.1, z: 3)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Neuroscience Warnings: PASS (+0.8, +0.4) — Clear evidence of cognitive decline.
- Student Boycotts: PASS (+0.7, +0.6) — Authentic grassroots pushback.
A study of 26,000 students in China revealed that while AI speeds up homework completion, monthly exam scores plummet, sparking youth boycotts and environmental protests in Tasmania.

The Bright Side:
Authentic student-led boycotts and grassroots movements are pushing back against predatory data centers and mindless technological adoption.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (homework speed) with WHO (deep cognitive development). The metric measures task output while destroying mental resilience.

Social Physics Analysis:
Tech platforms run a Smart Selfish Maneuver by selling cognitive shortcut tools that extract deep attention while manufacturing dependency and educational friction.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Unchecked automation hollows out human cognitive resilience.

The Unavoidable Truth: Offloading mental struggle to machines degrades the neural connections required for deep thought.

The Unavoidable Lie: AI assistants inherently enhance real learning and critical thinking.

Convenience is a silent tax on capability; trading cognitive struggle for speed forfeits the very foundation of human expertise.

It is deeply inspiring to see young people standing up for their right to think, learn, and feel deeply instead of outsourcing their minds to machines.
